es: Sopesar pruebas en equipo: proponer dos hipótesis con modales, descartar una con can't have y una razón, contrastar con la coartada y concluir citando la evidencia sin acusar de más.

teaching.en: The trophy is missing from the cabinet, and with no sign of a break-in we must narrow down the possible explanations one by one.
teaching.es: El trofeo ha desaparecido del armario y, sin señales de allanamiento, debemos acotar las explicaciones posibles una por una.
teaching.explanationEs: Planteamiento del caso: un dato y un método; narrow down = reducir las opciones.

teaching.en: One hypothesis is that the cleaner moved it to polish it; another is that it might have slipped behind the cabinet, which cannot be excluded yet.
teaching.es: Una hipótesis es que la persona de la limpieza lo movió para sacarle brillo; otra es que puede haberse deslizado detrás del armario, algo que aún no se puede excluir.
teaching.explanationEs: Dos hipótesis: might have + participio expresa lo posible, no lo seguro.

teaching.en: A stranger can't have taken it, because the door was locked all night and nobody saw anyone enter, so that hypothesis seems implausible.
teaching.es: Un extraño no puede haberlo cogido, porque la puerta estuvo cerrada con llave toda la noche y nadie vio entrar a nadie, así que esa hipótesis parece inverosímil.
teaching.explanationEs: Can't have + participio descarta: es casi imposible según la evidencia; implausible = inverosímil.

teaching.en: The cleaner has no alibi for Friday evening, and her keys can account for the fact that the cabinet shows no sign of damage.
teaching.es: La persona de la limpieza no tiene coartada para el viernes por la tarde, y sus llaves pueden explicar que el armario no muestre daños.
teaching.explanationEs: Account for = explicar un dato; alibi = prueba de que alguien estaba en otro lugar.

teaching.en: Since the cabinet is not broken, it must have been opened with a key, so my theory is that the cleaner moved the trophy.
teaching.es: Como el armario no está roto, debe de haberse abierto con una llave, así que mi teoría es que la persona de la limpieza movió el trofeo.
teaching.explanationEs: Must have + participio: conclusión casi segura apoyada en un dato.

teaching.en: If a colleague proposes a theory, say that could be true, but then test it against the evidence, for instance the locked door.
teaching.es: Si un compañero propone una teoría, di que podría ser cierta, pero luego contrástala con la evidencia, por ejemplo la puerta cerrada con llave.
teaching.explanationEs: Aceptar una idea no es darla por buena: se acepta como posible y se contrasta.

prompt.es: Elige la hipótesis posible, pero no segura.

choices.text: It must have been stolen by a stranger.
It can't be anywhere in the school.
It might have fallen behind the cabinet.

feedback.es: Might have + participio expresa una posibilidad; las otras frases afirman o niegan demasiado sin pruebas.

origin.text: The trophy is not in the cabinet, there are no signs of a break-in, and the cleaner says she did not touch it, although she was in the room on Friday.

prompt.es: Completa: «Un extraño no puede haberlo hecho, así que descartamos esa hipótesis.»

feedback.es: Can't have + participio descarta algo que, según la evidencia, es imposible en el pasado.

hint.es: Descarta con la forma negativa de can.

origin.text: The door was locked all night and only the cleaner has a key. A stranger ___ have done it, so we can rule out that hypothesis.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La persona de la limpieza debe de haber movido el trofeo.»

answer.text: The cleaner must have moved the trophy

feedback.es: Must have + participio expresa una conclusión casi segura sobre el pasado.

prompt.es: Escucha a Tom y elige qué hace con las pistas.

choices.text: He offers two explanations and admits their limits.
He is sure that the dog ate the cake.
He thinks that nobody came into the kitchen.

feedback.es: Con could have y might have ofrece dos explicaciones posibles, y reconoce que ninguna da cuenta de la ventana abierta.

origin.audio: Tom says the window was open, the cake is gone and there are small muddy prints on the table. The dog could have jumped up, or a child might have come in, but he admits that neither idea accounts for the open window.

prompt.es: Completa: «Puede que se haya caído» y «un extraño no puede haberlo cogido».

feedback.es: Might have expresa lo posible y can't have lo descarta: dos grados distintos de certeza.

sentences: It ___ have fallen behind the cabinet, but I am not sure.
The door was locked, so a stranger ___ have taken it.

prompt.es: Elige cómo rechaza Tom la idea de Sara apoyándose en un dato.

choices.text: That could be true, because the cleaner wasn't here this week.
That can't be right, because the cleaner wasn't here this week.
That must be right, because the cleaner wasn't here this week.

feedback.es: Rechazar una idea con un dato pide can't be right + because: si la persona de la limpieza no vino, no pudo moverlo.

origin.text: Sara suggests that the cleaner moved the trophy on Thursday, but Tom remembers that the cleaner was off work all week.

prompt.es: Escucha la reunión y elige qué advierte la directora al equipo.

choices.text: To question the two other teachers with keys immediately.
To stop looking for the trophy inside the building.
Not to blame the cleaner before the evidence is complete.

feedback.es: La directora pide no culpar aún a la persona de la limpieza: las pruebas son coherentes con que ella lo cogiera, pero no lo demuestran.

origin.audio: At the staff meeting, the head teacher described the case of the missing trophy. The cabinet had not been broken, she said, and the classroom door was locked all night, so a stranger seemed implausible. The cleaner, on the other hand, has a key and no alibi for Friday evening. Even so, the head teacher warned the team against blaming her yet: the evidence was consistent with the cleaner having taken it, but it did not prove it, and two other members of staff also have keys.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué actitud muestra la directora ante la culpa de la limpiadora.

choices.text: She considers it possible but not yet proved.
She is convinced that the cleaner is guilty.
She believes that the cleaner has a perfect alibi.

feedback.es: Dice que la evidencia es coherente con que la limpiadora lo cogiera, pero que no lo prueba: es posible, no demostrado.

prompt.es: Completa: «Podemos reducir la lista de sospechosos a tres personas.»

feedback.es: Narrow down significa reducir las opciones hasta quedarse con las más probables.

origin.text: Three people have a key: the cleaner and two teachers, so we can ___ down the list of suspects to three people, although none of them has admitted anything.

prompt.es: Escribe el caso: dos hipótesis, un descarte y una conclusión con pruebas.

answer.text: The trophy is missing from the cabinet, and I have two possible explanations. First, a stranger might have taken it during the night. Second, the cleaner could have moved it. Both ideas are possible at first, but only one of them fits the evidence. The door was locked all night, so a stranger can't have come in. In addition, the cabinet is not broken, which points to someone with a key. The cleaner has a key, came yesterday and has no alibi for Friday evening. On balance, the cleaner must have moved the trophy, although I can't be completely sure. The theory is plausible, but it would be unfair to accuse anyone yet, so we should ask the cleaner first.
accepted: The trophy is missing from the cabinet, and I have two possible explanations. First, a stranger might have taken it during the night. Second, the cleaner could have moved it. In addition, the cabinet is not broken, which points to someone with a key. The cleaner has a key, came yesterday and has no alibi for Friday evening. On balance, the cleaner must have moved the trophy, although I can't be completely sure. The theory is plausible, but it would be unfair to accuse anyone yet, so we should ask the cleaner first.

We have two possible explanations for the missing trophy. A stranger may have taken it, or the cleaner might have moved it. A stranger cannot have taken it, because the door was locked all night and the cabinet is not broken, so whoever opened it probably had a key. The cleaner has a key, worked yesterday and has no alibi for Friday evening. Since nothing else accounts for all the evidence, the most likely explanation is that the cleaner moved the trophy, perhaps to polish it. I am not certain, however, and it would be wrong to accuse her without proof. To be sure, we should ask the cleaner tomorrow and check who else holds a key.

feedback.es: El texto debe proponer dos hipótesis, descartar la del extraño por la puerta cerrada y concluir con la llave y la falta de coartada de la persona de la limpieza, proponiendo comprobarlo.

origin.text: Caso: ha desaparecido el trofeo del armario de la escuela. Pistas: (1) el armario no está roto; (2) la puerta del aula estuvo cerrada con llave toda la noche; (3) la persona de la limpieza tiene una llave, vino ayer y no tiene coartada para el viernes por la tarde. Escribe en inglés (160–210 palabras): propón dos hipótesis con might o could (un extraño y la persona de la limpieza), descarta una con can't have y explica por qué, concluye con must have o probably citando la evidencia y propón cómo comprobarlo.

prompt.es: Elige qué actitud muestra Mia ante el argumento de Leo.

choices.text: She rejects it completely and accuses someone else.
She accepts the point but asks for more proof.
She agrees and suggests calling the police now.

feedback.es: Mia dice que es posible, pero añade que cualquiera con la llave pudo abrir: acepta el punto y pide más pruebas, sin rechazarlo ni zanjar el caso.

origin.text: Leo argues that the cleaner must have taken the trophy because she has the key. Mia replies that this is possible, but the cabinet could also have been opened by anyone who had borrowed that key.

prompt.es: Completa: «Dos vecinos lo vieron cerca de la escuela, así que su coartada no se sostiene.»

feedback.es: Alibi es la versión con que alguien prueba que estaba en otro sitio; aquí la contradicen los vecinos.

origin.text: He says he was with friends on Friday evening, but two neighbours saw him near the school, so his ___ does not stand up.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Esa teoría es inverosímil porque no explica la puerta cerrada.»

answer.text: That theory is implausible because it cannot account for the locked door

feedback.es: Account for + dato: una hipótesis es inverosímil si no explica la evidencia.
